note: Unselected T2D; scored members are dulaglutide, semaglutide and danuglipron (exenatide and liraglutide are not members of this tile).
label: Type 2 diabetes (GLP-1R agonists)

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; model_first_use_year is the publication proxy.
engagement.note: Dulaglutide raised glucose-dependent insulin secretion in monkeys for up to a week after one dose; no human data yet.
engagement.short: Monkey insulin up for a week
engagement.quote: In monkeys, LY2189265 significantly increased glucose-dependent insulin secretion for up to a week after one dose, retained efficacy when administered subchronically (once weekly for 4 weeks) and was well tolerated.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of both papers; pairing is the drafter's.
engagement.note: Single doses in healthy volunteers raised glucose-dependent insulin secretion and blunted OGTT glucose at all doses, as in monkeys. Retro: GLP-1R agonists (exenatide, approved 2005) were already known to raise glucose-dependent insulin secretion in humans before the monkey data were public.
engagement.quote: Evidence of increase in glucose-dependent insulin secretion and suppression of serum glucose excursions were observed during an OGTT at all doses compared to placebo; no episodes of hypoglycaemia occurred.
engagement.judgement: Retro under the post-dating rule: engagement is a target claim, and human insulin secretion on GLP-1R agonists was public years before Glaesner 2010. Insulin secretion is downstream of receptor cAMP; no member has a direct occupancy readout. Healthy-volunteer data count for engagement. Paired by the drafter (same sponsor, no side-by-side statement).

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Candidate selection predates the 2015 paper; the year is the publication proxy.
dose.note: Semaglutide chosen as the once-weekly candidate on a 46 h i.v. half-life in minipigs.
dose.quote: The plasma half-life was 46.1 h in mini-pigs following i.v. administration, and semaglutide has an MRT of 63.6 h after s.c. dosing to mini-pigs.

dose.magnitude_basis: elimination half-life, human ~168 h vs minipig 46 h (3.6x longer in humans)
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Human t1/2 ~168 h (2017 label, https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/209637lbl.pdf) vs minipig 46 h. Earliest patient source is Kapitza 2015 (epub 2015-01-14); candidate selection on minipig PK predates the clinic but the model's first public date is Lau 2015 (epub Sept 2015).
dose.note: Women with T2D on weekly s.c. semaglutide up to 1.0 mg: PK compatible with once-weekly dosing, HbA1c -1.1%. Retro: this own-drug patient result (Jan 2015) was public before the minipig data (Sept 2015). Label (2017) gives t1/2 ~1 week.
dose.short: Weekly PK held in T2D; data came first
dose.quote: Semaglutide pharmacokinetics were compatible with once-weekly dosing; the semaglutide dose and dose-escalation regimen were well tolerated.
dose.judgement: Retro: dose is a claim about the drug, and semaglutide's own patient PK (Kapitza, Jan 2015) was public before the minipig half-life (Lau, Sept 2015). Reproduced: the once-weekly regimen held, half-life underpredicted 3.6x in the conservative direction (magnitude).

dose.note: Half-life 1.5-2 days in rats and monkeys; sponsor proposed once-weekly dosing on these data.
dose.quote: Half-life in rats and cynomolgus monkeys was 1.5-2 days, and serum immunoreactivity representing active compound persisted > 6 days.

dose.magnitude_basis: elimination half-life, human ~90 h vs rat/monkey 36-48 h (1.9-2.5x)
dose.note: Human half-life ~90 h supported once-weekly dosing; weekly doses >=1 mg lowered glucose and HbA1c in T2D (EGO, 5-week study).
dose.quote: LY showed an acceptable safety profile and exhibited the expected glucagon-like peptide-1 pharmacological effects on glucose suppression and insulin secretion with a half-life that supports once-weekly dosing.
dose.judgement: Half-life ratio straddles 2x (1.9-2.5x); recorded as off_by_2-5x. The regimen prediction held and patients were dosed to it with efficacy, so same rather than contra.

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; model_first_use_year from the 2020 bioRxiv of Griffith et al (doi:10.1021/acs.jmedchem.1c01856).
dose.note: Danuglipron does not act on rodent GLP-1R (primate Trp33); a humanized-receptor mouse showed efficacy comparable to injectable peptides.
dose.quote: We developed danuglipron (PF-06882961), an oral small-molecule GLP-1R agonist and found it had comparable efficacy to injectable peptidic GLP-1R agonists in a humanized mouse model.

dose.magnitude_basis: glycaemic efficacy relative to injectable peptides
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Year is the NCT03985293 results posting (2022-06-30), earlier than the 2023 paper. Quote is a clause of a longer sentence.
dose.note: Oral 120 mg b.i.d. cut HbA1c 1.16% vs placebo at 16 weeks, near the injectable range the mouse predicted.
dose.quote: For all danuglipron doses, HbA1c and FPG were statistically significantly reduced at week 16 vs placebo, with HbA1c reductions up to a least squares mean difference vs placebo of -1.16% (90% CI, -1.47% to -0.86%) for the 120-mg twice daily group
dose.judgement: No numeric exposure target from the mouse could be found at abstract level, so magnitude is direction_only. The 2025 discontinuation (liver injury, obesity programme) is a safety question, not dose, and was not scored (no model source on hepatic silence found).

dose.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: the dog work preceded the first-in-human trial NCT01037582 (first posted 2009-12-23); the review that reports it was public in 2019.
dose.quote: The ratio of 300 mg and 10mg semaglutide gave the greatest bioavailability, although great inter-animal variation was observed.
dose.note: Dog tablets: oral bioavailability 0.2-1.4%, highest with 300 mg SNAC; set the SNAC amount taken into humans.
dose.judgement: Opener dated to first use (before FIH), not to the review's publication.
dose.model: Beagle dog oral bioavailability of semaglutide/SNAC tablets

dose.magnitude_basis: oral bioavailability: dogs 0.2-1.4% vs humans 0.4-1% (label population PK); optimal SNAC 300 mg in both
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level for Granhall. registry_date is NCT01037582 first posting (no results posted). Human bioavailability from the 2019 Rybelsus label; oral 14 mg then met HbA1c in PIONEER.
dose.quote: In the single-dose trial, semaglutide exposure was highest when co-formulated with 300 mg SNAC.
dose.note: First-in-human: exposure peaked at 300 mg SNAC as in dogs; human oral bioavailability 0.4-1% sat within the dog range. Retro: oral semaglutide's own human data (phase 2, Davies 2017; FIH Granhall online 2018) were public before the dog study was (2019 FDA review).
dose.short: 300 mg SNAC optimal in humans too
dose.reason: Dog SNAC ratio and BA held
dose.judgement: Retro under the post-dating rule: dose is a claim about the drug, and the dog SNAC/bioavailability data were first public in the 2019 FDA review, after oral semaglutide's own human results. They reproduced the human SNAC optimum and bioavailability range. Paired by us (model side FDA review, patient side the FIH paper).
dose.model: Beagle dog oral bioavailability of semaglutide/SNAC tablets

efficacy.note: One dose improved glucose tolerance in diabetic mice; twice-weekly dosing for 4 weeks delayed hyperglycaemia and lowered weight.
efficacy.quote: LY2189265 increased glucose tolerance in diabetic mice after one dose and lowered weight and delayed hyperglycaemia when administered twice weekly for 4 weeks.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: HbA1c change (mice: glucose tolerance, no HbA1c)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. EGO's NCT number is not in the abstract; registry_date not found.
efficacy.note: EGO phase 2: once-weekly dulaglutide cut HbA1c 1.3-1.6% vs 0.24% placebo at 16 weeks; later semaglutide and danuglipron matched too. Retro: HbA1c lowering by GLP-1R agonists (exenatide 2005, liraglutide 2009) was public before the mouse data (2010).
efficacy.quote: At week 16, A1c changes (least-squares mean ± standard error) were -0.24 ± 0.12, -1.38 ± 0.12, -1.32 ± 0.12 and -1.59 ± 0.12%, in the placebo, LY 0.5/1.0, LY 1.0/1.0 and LY 1.0/2.0 arms, respectively (all p < 0.001 vs. placebo).
efficacy.reason: HbA1c fell in every member tested

patient_trials.quote: Mean baseline HbA1c was 8·05% (SD 0·85); at week 30, HbA1c significantly decreased by 1·45% (95% CI -1·65 to -1·26) with 0·5 mg semaglutide
For all danuglipron doses, HbA1c and FPG were statistically significantly reduced at week 16 vs placebo

efficacy.judgement: Retro under the post-dating rule: efficacy is a target claim and other GLP-1R agonists had lowered HbA1c in T2D trials before Glaesner 2010. Same, not neg: no member with model data is known to have missed its HbA1c primary endpoint (dulaglutide, semaglutide SUSTAIN 1, danuglipron phase 2b all positive). Outcome trial positive: SUSTAIN-6 (Marso 2016, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1607141) cut MACE with semaglutide. Discontinued members (LY2428757, TTP054, TTP273, CJC-1134-PC, YH14617) were not checked for HbA1c failures within budget.

efficacy.quote: We used these data to first compare associations of variants in genes encoding drug targets with the effects of pharmacological manipulation of those targets in clinical trials.
efficacy.note: Exome and genotyping in ~52,000 people tested a GLP1R missense variant as a proxy for receptor agonism. Genetic proxy tied to no drug: drug 'class'; compared with the class's glucose lowering across routes.
efficacy.short: GLP1R variant as genetic agonist proxy
efficacy.judgement: Opener at first use; the same paper already compares it with known trial effects (next entry).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: fasting glucose in carriers vs HbA1c fall on drug
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Glucose lowering by the class was known a decade earlier, so retro.
efficacy.quote: was associated with lower fasting glucose and T2D risk, consistent with GLP1R agonist therapies.
efficacy.note: Carriers had lower fasting glucose, reproducing the long-known glucose lowering of GLP-1R agonists.
efficacy.short: Variant lowers glucose like the drugs
efficacy.judgement: Retro, not same: the genetic proxy was run after member drugs had lowered HbA1c in trials.

efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC2928367). Pilot, nominal association.
efficacy.quote: One of these nonsynonymous SNPs, rs6923761 (which has a minor allele frequency of ∼29% in Caucasians), results in the substitution of serine for glycine at position 168 and may decrease responsiveness to infused GLP-1.
efficacy.note: 88 genotyped volunteers on GLP-1 infusion: Ser168 carriers had ~15% lower beta-cell responsivity, predicting weaker drug response. Infusion of native GLP-1, tied to no member drug; the compared patients took injected GLP-1 RAs.
efficacy.short: Ser168 carriers respond less to GLP-1
efficacy.judgement: Opener: a genotype-level prediction of which patients respond less to GLP-1-based therapy.
efficacy.model: GLP1R Gly168Ser genotype, GLP-1 infusion clamp in healthy volunteers

efficacy.magnitude_basis: HbA1c reduction per Ser168 allele vs beta-cell responsivity
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Pooled cohorts are mostly non-member drugs (liraglutide, exenatide, albiglutide in HARMONY); only AWARD dulaglutide is a member and its own estimate was not read. Effect too small to choose patients.
efficacy.quote: Variation in HbA1c reduction with GLP-1 receptor agonists treatment was associated with rs6923761G→A (Gly168Ser) in the GLP1R (0·08% [95% CI 0·04-0·12] or 0·9 mmol/mol lower reduction in HbA1c per serine, p=6·0 × 10-5)
efficacy.note: 4571 treated patients incl. AWARD (dulaglutide): each Ser168 allele gave a 0.08% smaller HbA1c fall, the direction the clamp predicted.
efficacy.judgement: Same at patient level on direction; low confidence because the member share of the pooled estimate is unknown. Dated to the online-first publication (Dec 2022; MEDLINE DateCompleted 2022-12-20), earlier than print (Jan 2023).
efficacy.model: GLP1R Gly168Ser genotype, GLP-1 infusion clamp in healthy volunteers

safety.confidence_note: On-target harm, pooled across modalities. Semaglutide's 2017 review reports the same at 0.4x clinical AUC in rats.
safety.note: Dulaglutide raised thyroid C-cell adenomas in 2-year rats at >=7x clinical AUC; FDA boxed warning, human relevance unknown.
safety.quote: In Sprague-Dawley rats, 2 years of twice weekly treatment resulted in an increase in the incidence of thyroid C-cell adenomas at >0.5 mg/kg (≥7X clinical AUC).

safety.magnitude_basis: thyroid cancer hazard ratio vs DPP4 inhibitors
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The cohort pools all GLP-1 RAs; the member (semaglutide, dulaglutide) share could not be read. Mean follow-up 3.9 years; MTC HR 1.19 (0.37-3.86) is uninformative.
safety.note: 145,410 GLP-1 RA users, 2007-21: no thyroid-cancer excess (HR 0.93); the rodent C-cell tumour prediction has not appeared in patients. Pooled cohort (members and non-members, same null); kept on the dulaglutide track the bioassay was filed for.
safety.quote: GLP1 receptor agonist use was not associated with increased risk of thyroid cancer (hazard ratio 0.93, 95% confidence interval 0.66 to 1.31; rate difference -0.13, 95% confidence interval -0.61 to 0.36 events per 10 000 person years).
safety.reason: Rodent C-cell tumours absent in patients
safety.judgement: Predicted harm not seen in patients scored contra/opposite per the brief. Alternative reading: untested, since MTC is rare and slow and the cohort is dominated by non-member liraglutide. Dissent exists (Bezin 2023, French case-control, not re-verified). Danuglipron's 2025 liver injury (obesity programme, tier 5) was not entered: no model source stating hepatic silence was found.

safety.confidence_note: Study date not in the review; year is the first public date (BLA review). Semaglutide's 2017 review reports the same monkey silence.
safety.quote: No treatment-related adverse microscopic findings were noted for the thyroid or parathyroid. There was no increase in the percentage of Ki67-labeled thyroid C-cells.
safety.note: Monkeys dosed at ~474x clinical AUC for a year showed no C-cell proliferation or calcitonin rise, unlike rats.
safety.short: No C-cell effect in monkeys at 474x AUC
safety.judgement: Opener: the sponsor ran the monkey study to argue humans respond like monkeys, not rats; a stated prediction of no human C-cell signal.

safety.magnitude_basis: mean serum calcitonin change vs placebo
safety.confidence_note: Patient readout is calcitonin, a C-cell biomarker; MTC itself is too rare for trials. Semaglutide MedR 2017 found no dose effect on calcitonin; Pasternak 2024 BMJ cohort (HR 0.93) is consistent and changes no status.
safety.quote: While neither dose of dulaglutide increased mean serum calcitonin compared to placebo, there were numerically more dulaglutide patients (n=6, 0.15%) with a calcitonin > 35 pg/ml than comparator patients (n=1, 0.05%).
safety.note: Dulaglutide phase 3: mean calcitonin did not rise vs placebo, as the monkeys predicted; a few outliers, most high at baseline.
safety.short: No mean calcitonin rise in patients
safety.judgement: Same, partial: mean calcitonin flat matches the monkey silence, but the reviewer notes numerically more >35 pg/ml outliers on drug. Paired by us across two documents of the same BLA.

safety.quote: The minor allele was also associated with protection against heart disease, thus providing evidence that GLP1R agonists are not likely to be associated with an unacceptable increase in cardiovascular risk.
safety.note: Variant carriers had less coronary heart disease: a prediction of no cardiovascular harm, possibly benefit.
safety.judgement: A stated cardiovascular-safety prediction, published June 2016 before any member drug's outcome trial.

safety.magnitude_basis: CHD in carriers vs MACE hazard ratio on semaglutide
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Novo Nordisk announced the SUSTAIN-6 MACE reduction on 2016-04-28 (press release), before Scott 2016 was published (2016-06-01). LEADER (liraglutide, not a member) topline was March 2016. registry_date is NCT01720446 results posting.
safety.quote: The primary outcome occurred in 108 of 1648 patients (6.6%) in the semaglutide group and in 146 of 1649 patients (8.9%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.95; P<0.001 for noninferiority).
safety.note: SUSTAIN-6: semaglutide met non-inferiority and cut MACE, as the variant predicted. Retro: the topline was public (press release 2016-04-28) before the genetics paper (June 2016).
safety.short: No CV harm; MACE fell on semaglutide
safety.judgement: Retro under the post-dating rule: for safety only the compared drug's own earlier result counts, and semaglutide's SUSTAIN-6 topline preceded the genetics paper. Non-inferiority CV outcome trial; the primary non-inferiority test governs and was met.

safety.magnitude_basis: CHD in carriers vs MACE hazard ratio on dulaglutide
safety.confidence_note: Abstract read. Year is the Lilly topline press release (2018-11-05), earlier than the Lancet paper (2019-06-09); registry_date is NCT01394952 results posting.
safety.quote: the primary composite outcome occurred in 594 (12·0%) participants at an incidence rate of 2·4 per 100 person-years in the dulaglutide group and in 663 (13·4%) participants at an incidence rate of 2·7 per 100 person-years in the placebo group
safety.note: REWIND: weekly dulaglutide 1.5 mg cut MACE vs placebo (HR 0.88, 0.79-0.99), as the variant predicted; dulaglutide's result came after the 2016 genetics paper.
safety.short: No CV harm; MACE fell on dulaglutide
safety.judgement: First prospective comparison after the retrodiction: dulaglutide's own CV outcome result was not public before Scott 2016. Paired by us.

safety.quote: In monkeys, LY2189265 significantly increased glucose-dependent insulin secretion for up to a week after one dose, retained efficacy when administered subchronically (once weekly for 4 weeks) and was well tolerated.
safety.note: Passing tolerability claim: once-weekly dulaglutide for 4 weeks was well tolerated in monkeys, scored as a safety prediction.
safety.judgement: A statement that the drug was well tolerated, made in an efficacy paper, is a safety prediction of that model.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; pairing is ours. Patients had nausea, diarrhoea and abdominal distension (13.8% each at the top dose) that the monkey summary does not mention.
safety.quote: LY2189265, given to overweight/obese patients with type 2 diabetes for 16 weeks in combination with OAMs, was relatively well tolerated and significantly reduced A1c, blood glucose and body weight.
safety.note: EGO (T2D on two oral agents): weekly dulaglutide up to 2 mg relatively well tolerated, GI events common; tolerability held, partially.
safety.judgement: Same, partial: patients tolerated the regimen as the monkeys did, but GI adverse events were frequent. Background oral agents are not a combination partner (placebo arm had them too).
